expected_approaches.summary: When unvisited land is found, traverse and mark its complete four-direction component.
expected_approaches.applicability: Finite rectangular grids with orthogonal adjacency.
key_invariants: A traversal marks every cell in its component before another count begins.
tradeoffs: Recursive DFS risks call-stack depth on large components.

expected_approaches.summary: Use a queue to mark each discovered component.
expected_approaches.applicability: Same grid traversal semantics with explicit queue storage.
key_invariants: A cell is marked when enqueued so it enters once.
tradeoffs: Avoids recursion depth but maintains a queue.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int numIslands(vector<string> grid){int m=grid.size(),n=m?grid[0].size():0,count=0;function<void(int,int)> dfs=[&](int r,int c){if(r<0||r>=m||c<0||c>=n||grid[r][c]!='1')return;grid[r][c]='0';dfs(r+1,c);dfs(r-1,c);dfs(r,c+1);dfs(r,c-1);};for(int r=0;r<m;r++)for(int c=0;c<n;c++)if(grid[r][c]=='1'){count++;dfs(r,c);}return count;} };

class Solution { public int numIslands(String[] grid){int m=grid.length,n=m==0?0:grid[0].length(),count=0;boolean[][] seen=new boolean[m][n];for(int r=0;r<m;r++)for(int c=0;c<n;c++)if(grid[r].charAt(c)=='1'&&!seen[r][c]){count++;fill(grid,seen,r,c);}return count;} void fill(String[] g,boolean[][] s,int r,int c){if(r<0||r==g.length||c<0||c==g[0].length()||s[r][c]||g[r].charAt(c)=='0')return;s[r][c]=true;fill(g,s,r+1,c);fill(g,s,r-1,c);fill(g,s,r,c+1);fill(g,s,r,c-1);} }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: A counted component cannot seed another island count.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Each cell is visited at most once.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Mark upon discovery to avoid repeat work.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Adding diagonal neighbors changes the traversal neighborhood.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why counting begins exactly once per component.

sample_phrasings: What exact condition begins a new island count?
How many islands are in [10,01] under this definition?
Why might you prefer iterative traversal for a very large island?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on visited timing and four-direction connectivity.

reference_reasoning: DFS and BFS flood fill are both strong valid priors; other correct component-traversal methods remain valid.
